newsitem.title: USA: Mobil says profits cut by special charges.
newsitem.headline: Mobil says profits cut by special charges.

text.p: Mobil Corp. said Monday its fourth-quarter profits fell nearly $100 million from a year ago because of special charges that included the start-up cost of its European marketing venture with British Petroleum.
The company said its net income fell to $676 million, or $1.68 a share, on revenues of $23.23 billion vs. year-earlier earnings of $775, or $1.93 a share, on revenues of $20.25 billion.

For the 1996 year, Mobil reported earnings of $3.0 billion, or $7.38 a share, on revenues of $80.78 billion. That compared with 1995 earnings of $2.37 billion, or $5.87 a share, on revenues of $75.37 billion.

The Fairfax, Va.-based company said its results for the latest quarter included a charge of $145 million to cover the start-up costs of a previously announced European marketing venture with British Petroleum.
It said that exploration and production profits for the latest quarter jumped $306 million to a record $649 million.
But earnings from marketing and refining fell $116 million to $256 million because of the higher cost of buying energy products.
Mobil said its chemicals unit's profits fell $59 million to $81 million for the quarter partly due to lower petrochemical margins.
Mobil's stock was up $1.375 at $130 on the New York Stock Exchange.
